walkthroughs.body_html:
Circles = female · Squares = male · Shaded = affected.

If two unaffected parents have an affected child, the allele must be recessive.

If every affected person has at least one affected parent, the allele is usually dominant.

Cystic fibrosis is recessive (ff). Two carrier parents (Ff × Ff) have a 1-in-4 chance per child.

Huntington's is dominant (Hh). One affected parent gives each child a 50% chance.

Screening can detect both — but raises tough choices.

The ABO gene has 3 alleles: Iᴬ, Iᴮ, Iᴼ.

Iᴬ and Iᴮ are codominant — both show together → blood group AB.

Iᴼ is recessive. So Iᴬ Iᴼ = group A, Iᴮ Iᴼ = group B, Iᴼ Iᴼ = group O.
